solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Silly dare — break in, getting apprehended by police

indicators.note: in tells us the break is placed inside the jumbled letters
silly suggests the letters of dare are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: a break is a rest

explanation.surface: A foolish dare to break into somewhere ends with the culprit being picked up by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the anagram signal; 'in' is the container signal, so the break word sits between the jumbled letters rather than after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being arrested is exactly being taken into custody by the police, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Take up music in school

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up means writing it from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a note is a piece of music in miniature

explanation.surface: A pupil is told to start studying music at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take up' reverses NOTE in this down entry. ETON College is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a well-known English public school, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Cut one of two pages out and tore to pieces

indicators.note: out tells us one of the letters is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: snipped means cut with scissors
P stands for page, and the longer word has two of them, so one goes

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a page out and rips the paper to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIPPED holds two Ps; 'out' removes one, giving a word that means criticised savagely.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to attack critically, so a critic who sniped at a work figuratively tore it to pieces.

clue.text: Did work on the farm — we had traps in now

indicators.note: traps means holds something inside, so the contracted we had encloses the other words

parts.note: we had is contracted to we'd, written without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Farm hands report that they've caught something in their traps just now.
explanation.walkthrough: WE'D (we had) 'traps' IN and NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating grain from chaff by blowing air through it is a traditional job in farming.

clue.text: Whyever set off before it's all over?

indicators.note: set off is read as disturbed or jolted, so the letters of whyever are rearranged

parts.note: ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone asks why on earth anyone would set out before the event has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like departing but is the anagram signal; 'all over' is the definition, not a sign of finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: All over can mean in every place, as in toys scattered all over the house.

clue.text: Seismic activity in epicentre more evident

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the following words
evident says the word can be seen there, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A report says the earthquake's effects are most visible at its epicentre.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across epicenTRE MORe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small earthquake or shaking of the ground is called this, so it is a kind of seismic activity.

clue.text: Squeezes casing … it works

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the squeezing word wraps round it

parts.note: wrings means twists and squeezes, as with wet washing

explanation.surface: Something squeezes its housing, and that is how the device works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a verb about the mechanism; it is the noun meaning an author's output.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's works are their written output, collectively their books and essays.

clue.text: Food, alas, upset diners — no stomach for it

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of alas are thrown into a new order
with no stomach the middle of diners is removed, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Sadly, the diners were put off their food and had no appetite for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALAS into SALA; 'no stomach' strips DINERS to DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes of mixed leaves and vegetables are a type of food.

clue.text: Still hiding, very upset

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the word for still holds the abbreviation

parts.note: inert means motionless or still

explanation.surface: Someone stays hidden, though deeply distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion; here it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something can mean to turn it upside down, the physical sense of overturning.

clue.text: Cruel people should be kept outside area

indicators.note: the people word stays outside, wrapped round the other letter

parts.note: men is a common crossword equivalent of people

explanation.surface: A call to keep unkind people out of the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe unkind or spiteful behaviour, a synonym of cruel.

clue.text: In a word, though there's been a volte face, nothing's changed

definitions.text: In a word, though there's been a volte face, nothing's changed

parts.words: In a word, though there's been a volte face, nothing's changed
parts.note: describes a word that reads the same when turned round end to end

explanation.surface: A commentator sums up: despite a U-turn, things are just as before.
explanation.walkthrough: A volte face is an about-turn; the clue describes a word unchanged when its letters run backwards, like LEVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as radar or kayak read identically in either direction, which is what the term names.

clue.text: Abet. Be expelled. Having done wrong, repented

indicators.note: expelled says the letters of be are thrown out of abet
done wrong means the letters of done are put the wrong way round, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer who aided a crime is expelled, and having done wrong, feels remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled' takes B and E out of ABET leaving AT; 'wrong' turns DONE into ONED.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for wrongdoing is a sign of having repented, a close synonym.

clue.text: Can't be frozen. That's obvious

definitions.meaning: read playfully as ..., impossible to turn into ice
plain to see or easy to spot

explanation.surface: Someone states that a thing cannot freeze and that this is self-evident.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into NOT ICE ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conspicuous enough to be spotted easily is obvious, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In day by day personal fight, going south

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces between the two abbreviations for day

parts.note: D again for day
own means personal, as in your own room
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: Someone describes a daily private struggle that is going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal: the two day abbreviations go on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Going south is idiom for heading down or worsening, so it means moving in a descending direction.

clue.text: Inessential, having crossed the Channel

parts.note: the clue asks for a word meaning superfluous that has come over from France

explanation.surface: Something deemed unnecessary has travelled across to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel is the English Channel, so the answer is a French phrase used in English, meaning too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means of too much, so it describes something superfluous or unwanted.

clue.text: Engaged plethora of actors for film. Dull

definitions.text: Engaged plethora of actors for film
definitions.meaning: read as hired too many players, cast to excess

explanation.surface: A producer hired far too many actors, and the resulting film was boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as OVER plus CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey sky completely covered with cloud is dull, a weather synonym.

clue.text: They reckon we may not see them hiding in the grass

definitions.meaning: people who add up figures, those who calculate

definitions.text: we may not see them hiding in the grass
definitions.meaning: snakes lurking unseen in long grass, notably vipers

explanation.surface: Someone warns that creatures hidden in the grass may go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is those who add sums; the other is the snake, Britain's only venomous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculators who add are reckoners, and the viper of that name hides in grassland.

clue.text: It's about protecting everyone riding a horse

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding to shield, so the reversed letters enclose the next piece
about signals turning the word round, read backwards

parts.note: it's written without its apostrophe
all means everyone
on means riding, as when you are on a horse

explanation.surface: Something is said to guard everyone who rides a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the reversal and 'protecting' the container; 'riding' gives a word meaning mounted upon.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse is a specific kind of horse.

clue.text: Why work out?

definitions.meaning: the cause or motive behind something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sceptic's question about exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is the explanation of why, and to think something through logically is to work it out.

clue.text: One will come up after fight and be taking minion into custody

definitions.text: One will come up after fight

indicators.note: taking means holding or absorbing, the first part of the instruction to enclose
into custody completes the picture of be holding the minion as a prisoner

parts.note: a lackey is a servile follower, a minion

explanation.surface: After a brawl, someone is told to arrest the underling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... into custody' is the container signal. 'come up' refers to a bruise rising after a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised eye socket appears after a punch, so this injury emerges after a fight.

clue.text: Pronounced groundbreaker in German music

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: a pioneer who goes first is a leader

explanation.surface: A pioneer in German music is said to be prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked; it signals that the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: These are German art songs for voice and piano, as by Schubert, so a form of German music.

clue.text: Are early settlers

parts.note: describes people who settle their bill ahead of time, before it is due

explanation.surface: A historical note about pioneers who arrived first in a land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlers' suggests colonists; here it means those who settle accounts, and they do so in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in advance is settling a bill early, which is what customers who do so are doing.

clue.text: Over and over disheartened minister

parts.note: past means over, as in the danger is over

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving just the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A clergyman who has lost heart again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves OR from OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a church minister, the clergyman in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Price of a suit?

parts.note: suit as a lawsuit, so its price is what the court case costs

explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests tailoring; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fees and expenses of a lawsuit are what such a case costs to bring or defend.

clue.text: Distance I left myself to cover

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap round, so the self word goes about the others

parts.note: me means myself

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a stretch they had to travel alone.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of length, 1760 yards, measures distance.

clue.text: Gracious! Half that is sheer fiction

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise like gracious

indicators.note: half takes just the first two letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: An exclaimed reaction: goodness, half of that is pure invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' gives TH from THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or invented story with no basis in fact is sheer fiction.

clue.text: Areas of factual writing

parts.note: real means factual or true
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A librarian lists the fields covered by non-fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Domains or fields of activity can be called areas, as in the realms of science.

clue.text: Choose one in twelve. It's mandatory

indicators.note: in places the choosing word and the numeral within the twelve word

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
opt means choose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rule that you pick one item from twelve, and it's compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve' means midday here, not the number, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is compulsory, you have no choice in the matter.
